comment: Thank you for taking the time to include input from the community in expanding the facilities as the Park City Sports Complex. As a parent of a figure skater who currently trains 12-14 hours per week, I would ask you to consider a second ice sheet to this complex. The only ice currently available from the Park City Ice Arena for our young figure skating athletes to train is before school beginning at 5:30am. Figure skating is the early morning side of this, but other ice sports are taking the late shift training until after 10pm at night. As you can imagine, this is not ideal for athletes who are also wanting to be at their best during a full school day. Please consider the effect this will have on so many young athletes in the early stages of the new development plan. The ice sports community has been actively proposing a solution to this problem for over a decade. The timing still seems right and definitely a prominent problem that is still top of mind when considering new facilities at the PC Sports Complex. My daughter skates on public ice sessions twice each week to get her training time in with limited ice availability. We often interact with visitors to our city who enjoy skating as a fun family friendly event. I think an additional ice sheet will serve the many athletes that dedicate countless hours as well as visitors to Park City for vacation, work, visiting family, etc.

comment: I’m excited about all new plans for Park City. We have wonderful town and people who care about their health and physical fitness. My daughter is a 15 y/old figure skater who needs to get up to get to ice rink 6xweek at 4.30 am as the only time the ice is available for figure skaters is early in the morning and sporadically in the afternoon. The ice time is divided between hockey and other ice activities and usually busy 20 h /day with very little public skating time. This creates very crowed and not always safe environment as it also limits young people potential and availability for visitors. I see a strong indication and need for another ice rink (seasonal at least) and I hope our voices will be heard as PC Figure Skating Club is growing bigger and stronger every year. We need PC to support your young community members as well as grieving interest of our visitors. Over last few years we have more visitors coming to ice rink for skating as our visitors often find it very rewarding, yet crowd starts to be as big as on the top of the mountains. We definitely need more ice rinks in PC. Please help us and future if PC.

comment: I am currently the girls and boys varsity soccer coach at PCHS. I write today to address an inequality that exists here in Park City as it relates to our high school girls' program. The girls' soccer program is the only high school field sport that due to the demands of football at Dozier Field during the fall have historically been moved off-site for trainings and games. With girls' soccer being a fall sport, we consistently run into issues regarding daylight on the Park City Sports Complex (Quinn's) Stadium Field. It is with that context that I strongly and emphatically urge you to approve the funding for lights at PC Sports Complex Stadium Field. In addition to the benefits to other sports programming in town, this approval would send a strong message that we in Park City value the participation and inclusion of girls and women's sports in our town. Yesterday being National Girls' and Women in Sports Day served as an important reminder that although Title IX was passed 50 years ago, access to equitable facilities and the necessary support continues to be a battle that girls and women are forced to confront on a daily basis. Funding these lights would also garner additional support, make our games more of a community event and enable parents and families that are not currently able to attend afternoon games due to work more accessible. I thank you for your consideration and your service to our community. I'm available to discuss this further if you have any additional questions regarding the importance of this initiative as we continue to champion the benefits of lifelong physical literacy and the benefits of team sports and civic pride in Park City.

comment: I am a parent of a figure skater and a former board member of the Figure Skating Club of Park City. The potential for expanding recreation opportunities at Quinn's Junction is very exciting. So first, thank you to everyone who has worked on the Master Plan to get us to this point. The Park City skating community (figure skating, hockey, curling, school programs - all of us) feel the impacts of limited ice time every day. While this is truly a year-round issue, winter comes with additional challenges in the form of private rentals, tournaments, and events that make it even more difficult for skaters to train sufficiently (and at reasonable hours). My 12-year-old was hoping to attend this meeting and provide a comment in person, but she has to wake up at 4:30am on Fridays, as freestyle ice is only programmed between 5:30 and 7:30am (with one additional hour later during school hours). So she will be trying to get to sleep while public comments begin tonight. On the other end of the rink's operating hours, I recently was made aware that a hockey game would be starting at 11pm tonight. I think it goes without saying that a second ice sheet, even seasonally, would alleviate some of the programming and training challenges for a rink that is currently programmed 19.5 hours a day. I also believe that a seasonal outdoor rink aligns perfectly with the interests of our community and winter visitors - who come to Park City from around the world to experience our winter sports town. Please consider including the seasonal rink in the early phases of planning for this exciting development opportunity.

comment: I live at 988 W Abigail Drive, Kamas, Utah. I do not live, and never have lived in Hideout (though at least one member of the Council has repeatedly told people I do). The PC MARC is a wonderful facility. I have been going there from the time I moved here in Dec, 2014. It was great when I was a tennis player, and absolutely horrible when I became a pickleball player. The Racquet Club was built decades ago as a private tennis club. Park City bought it, and in 2010 did a great job of renovating and expanding it. Sadly, because of the attitudes of its Director, Ken Fisher, it is being run in 2023 as if it were still a private tennis club. PB players are afforded little opportunity to book courts in the bubble. We not only get very few hours, but also only the worst hours – when it opens at dawn or the evening hours before it closes. PB players are never able to book a bubble court during “prime time”. Not ever. Mr. Fisher has misled the City Council by providing incomplete information and offering indefensible rationalizations for this. He has said repeatedly that tennis brings in far more revenue, and thus should get the most hours. But as I have told the Council before, if you do a deeper dive, you will see: • Tennis court reservation revenue dropped by over $28K last year • Growth in tennis revenue was attributable to lessons, not court bookings • PB court reservation revenue rose by over $22K last year (despite the paucity of hours and the worst possible times). • PB total revenue is up over 400% in the last two years • Tennis does not get more hours because it brings in more money; it brings in more money because it gets far more – and better- hours Mr. Fisher and RAB liaison Max Doilney have offered as a second rationale that the MARC is a “purpose built” facility, and that its primary purpose was and should continue to be tennis. I previously shared an Op Ed I wrote for the Park City Record in which that argument was dismantled. Further, I ask the Council to consider if the use of a public facility in 2023 should be determined by the purpose for which it was built – as a private tennis club – decades ago. Finally, I ask whether a Council that meets in a repurposed school should cling to the absurd notion that a facility’s use should be dictated by the purpose for which it was first built. I have repeatedly asked this body to look at how many times bubble courts go unbooked. We get e-mails from Cole Johnson several times a week notifying us that the MARC has opened courts for PB the next day. Bear in mind that we only get these e-mails if every court is open. If two people are playing singles on one bubble court, 16 people are blocked from playing PB. Is this the best use of public courts? How much money is the MARC losing? In his Nov 3, 2022 Report to the City Council, Ken Fisher identified 3 things the MARC was doing “to accommodate the growing demand by the pickleball community for access to indoor tennis courts”. Let’s take a closer look. Number 1 on Ken’s list was giving PB players more hours for drop in play in the gym. Clearly more hours in the gym does not give PB players greater access to the indoor tennis courts. It is completely unresponsive. Number 2 on Ken’s list was releasing unused tennis courts at 11 AM the day before rather than 11 AM the same day. This is completely misleading and entirely unacceptable. First, the MARC only releases bubble courts if all three are empty. Again, remember that if two people are playing singles tennis on one court, the MARC does not release the other two courts. They sit unused. Second, tennis players have had one full week to book bubble courts; PB players get one day. This is blatantly unfair. Number 3 on Ken’s list was ending the right of PB players to reserve courts from 7-10 PM on Tuesday and Thursday. He instead dedicated those hours to “open play” and allowed up to 48 people to sign up, even though only 24 can play at a time. Taking away court reservation hours and converting them to “open play” is quite literally robbing Peter to pay Paul. PB players got no added hours. Indeed, In my old days as a consumer lawyer, we would have referred to this as a scam – double booking the same space and charging twice for something half the buyers are unable to use. Attached is a picture taken on Tuesday, Jan. 24. That evening at least 35 people paid $10 each to play “open pickleball”. There were always 11 people shut out at any given time, waiting for their “opportunity” to play. This happens regularly. Every time a game ends, 4 players walk off their court, interrupting the play of every court they must cross to put their paddles in the slots awaiting their turn. Then 4 other players walk across the court, again interrupting play as they head to the open court. This happens continuously. Because the number of people and the distribution of skill levels is random, the games are almost always worse. You invariably are forced to either “play up” (play with people better than you) or “play down” (play with people worse than you). Either way it ruins the game. The PB players are charged more money ($10 instead of $8.50), they play fewer games (because of all the time they must sit out) and the games are of lesser quality / enjoyment. And it takes 3 hours instead of 2. Ken often says he does not want to “degrade the tennis experience” but seems to be perfectly happy to completely degrade the PB experience on Tuesday and Thursday nights. Many of us have stopped going. And over 120 members of the PCPB Club have joined the private club in Sandy. I wonder why the MARC did not institute “open play” for tennis players…could it be because they (quite rightly) would never stand for it? This is how Ken Fisher has “accommodated the growing demand by the pickleball community for access to indoor tennis courts”. He has done nothing of the sort. Your own survey showed demand for PB courts (26.5%) nearly double the next two items respondents listed – year round trails (13.8%) and cross country ski trails (13.5%). You clearly recognize the huge demand for indoor PB courts, as it has prompted a significant investment in the Quinns Junction project. And yet the MARC continues to give PB players even fewer opportunities to book a bubble court than we had last year – all while tennis courts often sit empty. It’s time to run the MARC like a public municipal and recreational facility – not like the private tennis club it used to be. You can take action NOW to remedy the injustice while we await construction of new facilities. The aspirational goal of new dedicated indoor PB courts in 3 or 4 years is no excuse for doing nothing today. PB deserves parity, now. Here are some immediate steps that the Council can take tomorrow: • Give PB players an opportunity to book bubble courts during “prime time

comment: I am writing to express my support for enhancements being considered as they relate to Nordic ski facilities at Quinn's. My family moved to town in the early 2000s and during that first winter fell in love with cross country skiing. Currently, we have three kids participating on the PCSS Nordic Team- one on Comp and two in the Devo program. I also volunteer my time 3 days a week to the club as a PCSS coach. As you know, cross country skiing is very popular in our town and continues to grow significantly year over year. It is an all-ages, all-abilities, life-long sport, and unlike most other winter activities, is more broadly accessible to all of our community members across the socio-economic spectrum. Emma Garrard and the Nordic team have done an amazing job creating opportunities, and this year I understand that 45% of participants of the "next generation" Mini Gliders, the youngest members of the PCSS Nordic program, are of our Latinx community, directly supporting City Council's mission for social equity and involvement. I have witnessed many improvements to our community's xc skiing experience over the years, and in particular, through our community's open space organizations/initiatives, and Mountain Trails and Basin Rec which do a remarkable job in grooming, maintaining and enhancing the public trails system. Currently, however, our community lacks several public infrastructure elements as they relate to xc skiing, which can be addressed via improvements at Quinn's. Our community would greatly benefit from a Nordic center where participants could gather, have a snack, stretch, prep their equipment, use the restroom, etc. This facility would be used year-round- during the winter by skiers/bikers/hikers, and during the summer by bikers/hikers. Centers such as this exist in many premier cross-country communities. Adjacent to this facility should be novicelevel trails and a groomed open space that can support newer skiers/kids as they learn and play games on skis (such as "sharks and minnows", which in addition to being fun for the kids during practice, it is an extremely effective method leveraged by xc coaches around the world for helping kids improve their agility and become better skiers). Additionally, positioning the Nordic center/parking on the "trails" side of the road will address safety and usability concerns that currently exist. As required now, skiers must tote equipment, and walk dogs across the road from the parking area. I've witnessed close calls and know of dogs that have gotten hit. This situation is especially dangerous for children, who are often crossing at 545 pm in the winter as the sun is setting, and where drivers are leaving the Ice Arena and navigating around the corner on Gillmor Way. Thank you for your time and your consideration as you contemplate and approve enhancements to PCSC at Quinn’s Junction.

comment: As a figure skating club member that has been a part of the sport for over 12 years, I would like to kindly remind the council that we are still here. I was here almost a decade ago when plans fell through for an additional rink. Now everyday we must wake up at 4:30 or earlier, just to get the ice time we need. Not only has this issue impacted the figure skaters, but also all others from the skating community. Our rink operates almost 20 hours a day to accommodate the demand for ice time. Especially during the winter months, private parties and rentals take away precious training hours. Please consider the skating community and add a seasonal rink in your preliminary plans.

We hope that you will consider making another rink for use for our many skaters in the Wasatch back including Summit County. We have skaters coming from Park City, Coalville and Heber. comment: Since there is nothing that I feel I can add to the letter so eloquently written by Ms. Farkas, I would simply like to state that I agree to every aspect of her letter. Simply, we need more quality ice and ice times in Park City. I too have skated for a number of years and have struggled over the past year to enjoy the sport due to the limited ice times available. I think it’s important for me to state that for many of my skating peers, skating is not just a sport but rather an essential part of our mental and physical wellbeing. I was a little stunned that this fee would be increased when the sessions have been decreased. It is important to understand that some of us still work and can’t make it to every session, we simply need more options. So in closing, I hope that you will consider the current demand for ice that is simply not being met at this time.

comment: I am writing to plead the council's approval for the critical need for additional ice at the Quinn's Junction Ice Arena. The community has long outgrown this facility. I am also writing in particular about the segment of the community that is underserved by the lack of available public ice sessions. I have skated weekly at this arena for the past 17 years - ice skating is a sport that promotes both physical and mental well being. This year-round rink was a major factor in why I chose to make Park City my year round home. Sadly, the available ice time has become very, very limited for public use. And, as I am now a senior skater, it is not appropriate for me to skate at the competitive ice times for free -style skate sessions. So, I am writing on behalf of a number of peer, adult skaters and new skaters that have expressed concerns to PC rink management about the lack of scheduling, timing and duration for public skate sessions. The Park City ice rink and staff have done an exceptional job over the years of providing a full-service arena for many different skating disciplines. But it has long ago outgrown its current size. We desperately need more ice surface to provide a safe and enjoyable environment for all that want to enjoy this sport and grow in this sport. As an adult senior skater it has become almost impossible for me to feel comfortable on the ice when so many people and types of skaters are using the ice... from hockey players, to freestyle jumpers, to beginners! It's simply nerve racking and unsafe. As Park City continues to aspire to serve its sports minded community, it now needs to address the growing need of the ice skating community of all ages and disciplines. Thank you for considering these comments and hopefully your decision to move forward with an additional ice sheet to meet the needs of the community.

comment: I am writing on behalf of the Park City Soccer Club in support of lighting the Stadium field at PC Sports Complex. Living in a mountain environment, long shadows impact the visibility on our fields much earlier than elsewhere. By September 1 we have sunset at 8pm and there are very few venues for our teams to host games during our Fall League season, or train in the late evening other times of the year. Currently, the only lit fields available to our youth are the turf and “D” fields at the Park City Sports Complex; I would image priority given to PC Rec adult rec league activities is why we are never scheduled at City Park. Even at Quinn’s, we find ourselves competing for lit fields with the adult kickball, softball and 7 v 7 soccer programs, not to mention high school sports, youth lacrosse, and even other soccer programs. Due to a shortage of soccer referees statewide, we are directed by our State Association to schedule weeknight games back-to-back, creating the most efficiency in sending teams of referees to Park City. However, with a 5:30 start for the first game, and games lasting anywhere from 75-90 minutes, we spend most of the Fall season (late August through early November) trying to schedule and re-schedule games for our teenaged teams on just two fields across our whole community; these games are usually restricted to 2 nights per week at that. A third lit field would make a significant difference. We truly believe that the recent study does not accurately represent the frustration and desire for lit fields among our 500+ families. The majority of our membership is comprised of young active families, juggling soccer practice with other activities, then racing home for dinner, homework or family time. Advocacy just does not rate as a priority, and they certainly do not have the same leisure time to attend City Council meetings as some of the other sports clubs seeking to be heard in our community.

comment: I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the new facilities being developed at Quinn's junction. I would like to extend my gratitude to all those who have contributed their time and effort to make this project a reality. My daughter, who is a figure skater, has been a part of the club for several years now and we have witnessed the overwhelming demand for ice time that greatly surpasses the existing capacity. As you may be aware, the current ice schedules are quite demanding, with hockey games starting as late as 11pm and skaters hitting the ice as early as 5:30am before school. Despite these challenges, the skating community continues to grow and attract skaters from all over the country to come train. It is for this reason that I am writing to you to request your support in considering a seasonal rink in the early phases of planning. Approximately 10-12 years ago, the skating community rallied for another rink, and the city did listen. However, with the promise of a rink at Black Rock by private developers, the push for the second sheet was put on hold. Now, 10 years later, with no additional ice and more skaters at higher levels, the need for another rink is more pressing than ever. As a winter sports community that attracts visitors from around the world, a seasonal outside rink, equipped with refrigeration to ensure proper ice conditions, aligns well with the interests of our community and visitors. The rink would not only alleviate the stress of scheduling and demanding ice time, but it would also provide more opportunities for our residents and visitors to enjoy winter activities. I believe that the addition of a seasonal rink would greatly benefit the community and I urge you to give it your consideration.

comment: About a decade ago a group of figure skaters wearing their dresses came to council meeting and asked city council to solve the limited ice problem at the Park City Ice Arena. Nothing happened. Since then, our skaters have adjusted. Olympic figure skating hopefuls as young as 8-year-old are waking up at 4:30am to get fed, warmed up, and on the ice to train by 5:30am. This is a very hard and unsustainable schedule for these elite athletes. As the council considers recreational opportunities at the Sports Complex at Quinn’s the skaters would like to remind them that we are still here, the need for more ice has only increase since the last time we skated into the chambers. As you consider new requests for recreation we kindly ask that you keep the figure skaters/curlers/speed skaters/public skaters/hockey skaters/sledge hockey/ and all other ice aficionados in mind during the preliminary stages of your planning.
